feature: Size mode measures avatars, icons and stacks, and a rough box snaps to the thing inside it
summary: In the Measure tool's Size mode, hovering a round avatar, an icon tile, a pill or count badge, or one avatar in a stack now outlines that thing at its true size, and ] steps out to the whole stack. Dragging a rough box round something measures what is wholly inside it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Open a screenshot with avatars (the walk uses Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/people-panel-2x.png; walk: Scripts/playtest/size-reads-avatars-and-stacks-walk.json).

try.do: Press I until the Mode reads Size, then rest the pointer on a round photo avatar.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click: the width and height land, 32 by 32 for a 32 point avatar.
Rest on one avatar in a stack, then press ] to take in the whole stack.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press I to get Size back, then drag a loose box round one avatar in the stack and watch the outline before you let go.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag a loose box round the whole stack and let go.
Drag a box round empty space: the box is measured as drawn and a notice says Kept your box.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: On your own Teams or Slack screenshots, does hovering an avatar now outline the avatar rather than a piece of it or the whole row?
Is ] the way out from one avatar to the stack you expected, or would you reach for something else?
When you drag a rough box, does the live outline tell you what you will get before you let go?
Should an empty box be kept as drawn, or would you rather nothing landed?
After a Size click the tool goes back to Select, so each box needs Size picked again: is that in your way here?
rough: Tested on a rendered 2x people panel with known sizes (photo, pale and initials avatars, a presence dot, a four-avatar stack with a +3 pill, icon tiles, two badges, a photo in a card), not on a real Teams or Slack capture, which this machine cannot take for the loop.
Shapes are told apart from their background by brightness alone: an avatar the same brightness as the page behind it is not seen.

Avatars in a stack are read one by one because the stack draws a ring of page colour round each; a stack drawn with no ring, avatars touching, is expected to read as one piece on hover (not yet tried).
A shape bigger than 160 points from the pointer either way is left to the old reader, which measures panels and cards as before.
The bordered Save button still reads 78 by 26 against its true 80 by 28: that is the old reader's number, kept on purpose so nothing that read before moves; the new reader would say 80 by 28.
No mock covers the rough box gesture.
The hover outline matches the redline mock's highlight, as before.
